packet.headline_seed: Orange haze from Canada wildfires seen in Ontario and northern US
packet.description_seed: There are currently 838 wildfires actively burning across the country, according to the Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre.

what: Orange haze from Canada wildfires seen in Ontario and northern US

clean_source_blocks.text: Smoke from wildfires burning across Ontario and Manitoba is spreading over the northern United States this week, prompting air quality alerts in at least four states and reduced visibility in several others. The Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre said 836 wildfires were active nationwide as of Tuesday, with 194 classified as out of control, concentrated in the Northwest Territories, Ontario and Quebec. The National Weather Service issued air quality alerts for Michigan, Minnesota, Wisconsin and Colorado tied to the smoke, while conditions were also deteriorating in parts of New York. The Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy issued a statewide alert for Wednesday, warning that air quality could reach the "unhealthy for sensitive groups" category, with pockets of "unhealthy" air possible closer to the Canadian border. A similar alert was extended into Thursday.

Millions of Americans could see hazy skies and worsening air quality over the next few days as smoke from hundreds of wildfires burning across Canada spreads across the Midwest, Great Lakes and Northeast. More than 830 wildfires were burning across Canada as of Wednesday, with some of the largest blazes in west-central Ontario sending thick plumes of smoke south into the United States, according to ABC News. The smoke will first impact the Upper Midwest before expanding east into the Great Lakes, Ohio Valley, Mid-Atlantic and Northeast through Thursday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. Around 100 million people in the U.S. could experience at least some effects, though conditions will vary by location.

For the latest wildfire counts, evacuation orders, air quality updates and how the fires are affecting Ontarians, follow Yahoo Canada's live blog below. Ontario's wildfire situation remains at a critical stage Wednesday evening, with more than 100 fires burning across the province and over half considered out of control. Several communities in northwestern Ontario remain under evacuation orders as crews battle rapidly changing conditions, while smoke from the fires continues to drift south, worsening air quality across much of southern Ontario Wildfire activity remains intense across northwestern Ontario, with 148 active fires burning across the region as of Wednesday evening, according to data shared on the provincial wildfire dashboard. Of those, 69 fires remain out of control, while crews have contained or are monitoring the remaining blazes. Collins First Nation (Namaygoosisagagun First Nation)

A stretch of extreme heat has supercharged Ontario's wildfire season, with more than 100 active fires burning across the northern region of the province and forcing residents from their homes in parts of northwestern Ontario. Residents have flooded social media with apocalyptic images and videos of towering flames, smoke-filled skies and ash-covered communities as wildfires burn across northwestern Ontario. The smoke has travelled hundreds of kilometres south, pushing air quality readings in parts of southern Ontario to among the worst in the world. Residents in several northwestern Ontario communities have been ordered to evacuate as fires continue to spread, with some escaping by boat while dramatic footage showed flames engulfing the landscape around a CN Rail train helping evacuate residents.

payload.title: Kanadan maastopalojen savu värjäsi taivaan oranssiksi ja heikensi ilmanlaatua Yhdysvalloissa
payload.summary: Ontarion ja Manitoban maastopaloista kulkeutunut savu on aiheuttanut ilmanlaatuvaroituksia Yhdysvalloissa. Ontarion luoteisosissa useita yhteisöjä on määrätty evakuoitaviksi.
payload.content:
Kanadan Ontariossa ja Manitobassa riehuvien maastopalojen savu on kulkeutunut tällä viikolla satoja kilometrejä etelään, värjännyt taivasta oranssiksi Ontariossa ja Yhdysvaltain pohjoisosissa sekä heikentänyt ilmanlaatua laajalla alueella. Kanadassa oli keskiviikkona käynnissä yli 830 maastopaloa, ja savun arvioitiin voivan aiheuttaa lähipäivinä ainakin jonkinlaisia vaikutuksia noin 100 miljoonalle yhdysvaltalaiselle, vaikka olosuhteet vaihtelevat alueittain.

Evakuointeja Ontarion luoteisosissa

Ontarion luoteisosan tilanne oli keskiviikkoiltana kriittinen. Maakunnan maastopalojen seurantatietojen mukaan alueella oli 148 aktiivista paloa, joista 69 oli hallitsemattomia. Muut palot oli saatu hallintaan tai niitä seurattiin. Useita yhteisöjä koskivat evakuointimääräykset, kun sammutusmiehistöt työskentelivät nopeasti muuttuvissa oloissa. Osa asukkaista pakeni veneillä, ja kuvamateriaalissa liekit ympäröivät asukkaiden evakuointiin osallistunutta CN Railin junaa.

Pitkittynyt äärimmäinen kuumuus on voimistanut Ontarion palokautta, ja maakunnan pohjoisosissa paloi yli sata aktiivista maastopaloa. Savu on kulkeutunut satojen kilometrien päähän eteläiseen Ontarioon, jossa ilmanlaatu on paikoin laskenut maailman heikoimpien joukkoon. Asukkaiden jakamissa kuvissa ja videoissa näkyi korkeita liekkejä, savun täyttämää taivasta ja tuhkan peittämiä yhteisöjä.

Savu leviää Yhdysvalloissa itään

Kanadan metsäpalokeskuksen mukaan maassa oli tiistaina 836 aktiivista maastopaloa, joista 194 luokiteltiin hallitsemattomiksi. Palot keskittyivät etenkin Luoteisterritorioihin, Ontarioon ja Quebeciin. Keskiviikkona maanlaajuinen määrä oli yhä yli 830, ja osa suurimmista paloista sijaitsi Ontarion länsi- ja keskiosissa. Paksut savupilvet nousivat muun muassa näistä paloista sekä Manitoban paloalueilta ja siirtyivät ensin Yhdysvaltain Keskilännen pohjoisosiin. Yhdysvaltain meri- ja ilmakehähallinnon ennusteen mukaan savun oli määrä levitä torstaihin mennessä Suurten järvien alueelle, Ohion laaksoon, Keski-Atlantin osavaltioihin ja Koilliseen.

Yhdysvaltain kansallinen sääpalvelu antoi savun vuoksi ilmanlaatuvaroituksia Michiganissa, Minnesotassa, Wisconsinissa ja Coloradossa. Ilmanlaatu heikkeni myös osissa New Yorkin osavaltiota, ja savu vähensi näkyvyyttä useilla muilla alueilla. Michiganin ympäristöviranomainen antoi koko osavaltiota koskevan varoituksen keskiviikoksi ja jatkoi sitä torstaille. Ilmanlaadun arvioitiin voivan olla herkille väestöryhmille epäterveellistä, ja lähempänä Kanadan rajaa mahdollisia olivat paikoin kaikille epäterveelliset olot. Savun vaikutusten laajuuden ja voimakkuuden arvioitiin vaihtelevan alueittain.
summary_bullets: Kanadassa oli keskiviikkona aktiivisena yli 830 maastopaloa.
Ontarion luoteisosassa 69 paloa oli keskiviikkoiltana hallitsemattomia.
Savun vuoksi annettiin ilmanlaatuvaroituksia ainakin neljässä Yhdysvaltain osavaltiossa.

Ilmanlaatu heikkeni myös osissa New Yorkin osavaltiota, ja savu vähensi näkyvyyttä useilla muilla alueilla. Michiganin ympäristöviranomainen antoi koko osavaltiota koskevan varoituksen keskiviikoksi ja jatkoi sitä torstaille. Ilmanlaadun arvioitiin voivan olla herkille väestöryhmille epäterveellistä, ja lähempänä Kanadan rajaa mahdollisia olivat paikoin kaikille epäterveelliset olot. Savun vaikutusten laajuuden ja voimakkuuden arvioitiin vaihtelevan alueittain.

Smoke from wildfires burning across Ontario and Manitoba is spreading over the northern United States this week, prompting air quality alerts in at least four states and reduced visibility in several others. The Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre said 836 wildfires were active nationwide as of Tuesday, with 194 classified as out of control, concentrated in the Northwest Territories, Ontario and Quebec. The National Weather Service issued air quality alerts for Michigan, Minnesota, Wisconsin and Colorado tied to the smoke, while conditions were also deteriorating in parts of New York. The Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy issued a statewide alert for Wednesday, warning that air quality could reach the "unhealthy for sensitive groups" category, with pockets of "unhealthy" air possible closer to the Canadian border. A similar alert was extended into Thursday.

Millions of Americans could see hazy skies and worsening air quality over the next few days as smoke from hundreds of wildfires burning across Canada spreads across the Midwest, Great Lakes and Northeast. More than 830 wildfires were burning across Canada as of Wednesday, with some of the largest blazes in west-central Ontario sending thick plumes of smoke south into the United States, according to ABC News. The smoke will first impact the Upper Midwest before expanding east into the Great Lakes, Ohio Valley, Mid-Atlantic and Northeast through Thursday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. Around 100 million people in the U.S. could experience at least some effects, though conditions will vary by location.

For the latest wildfire counts, evacuation orders, air quality updates and how the fires are affecting Ontarians, follow Yahoo Canada's live blog below. Ontario's wildfire situation remains at a critical stage Wednesday evening, with more than 100 fires burning across the province and over half considered out of control. Several communities in northwestern Ontario remain under evacuation orders as crews battle rapidly changing conditions, while smoke from the fires continues to drift south, worsening air quality across much of southern Ontario Wildfire activity remains intense across northwestern Ontario, with 148 active fires burning across the region as of Wednesday evening, according to data shared on the provincial wildfire dashboard. Of those, 69 fires remain out of control, while crews have contained or are monitoring the remaining blazes. Collins First Nation (Namaygoosisagagun First Nation)

A stretch of extreme heat has supercharged Ontario's wildfire season, with more than 100 active fires burning across the northern region of the province and forcing residents from their homes in parts of northwestern Ontario. Residents have flooded social media with apocalyptic images and videos of towering flames, smoke-filled skies and ash-covered communities as wildfires burn across northwestern Ontario. The smoke has travelled hundreds of kilometres south, pushing air quality readings in parts of southern Ontario to among the worst in the world. Residents in several northwestern Ontario communities have been ordered to evacuate as fires continue to spread, with some escaping by boat while dramatic footage showed flames engulfing the landscape around a CN Rail train helping evacuate residents.
